thesis_summary.thesis: Abacus Global Management (NYSE: ABX; notes: ABXL) is an alternative-asset and life-settlement platform. **[Fact]** The company originates and brokers purchases of life insurance policies between policy sellers and institutional buyers, services those policies until mortality, and earns spread plus fees. **[Fact]** It also runs asset-management sleeves (including free-cash-flow-themed strategies via FCF Advisors, acquired December 2024) and a small technology services line (Abacus Intel mortality verification, launched late 2024). **[Fact]** Revenue is reported in three segments: Life Solutions, Asset Management, and Technology Services. **[Fact]** The company renamed from Abacus Life, Inc. in February 2025 and lists on the NYSE with 9.875% senior notes due 2028 (ABXL).
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: Life-settlement economics are opaque: GAAP net income can look modest while adjusted earnings and policy-portfolio marks tell a stronger story. **[Inference]** FY2025 revenue rose to $235 million (+110% year over year) and adjusted EBITDA reached $133 million, yet FY2025 cash from operations was only $26 million because policy purchases and working capital absorb cash before mortality payoffs arrive. **[Inference]** The stock near $9.25 (~2.2 times GAAP book) may screen expensive on trailing GAAP free cash flow while underpricing a rollup that doubled revenue through Carlisle and FCF Advisors. **[Inference]** Complexity (fair-value policy portfolio, securitized funding, dual equity/note structure) may keep generalist investors away even when servicing fees and securitization are repeatable.
